text:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

Hard to overstate how big of a deal this is.

tl;dr — ANY unpatched Linux server with even a single TCP port exposed to the internet (say for HTTP or SSH) and MPTCP active (default for many Go web servers) is vulnerable to complete takeover.

text:
This is why I said you want your VPS ports all closed

Then only let it be accessible inside your Tailscale for SSH and via a Cloudflare Tunnel to receive web traffic

Any Linux box can be taken over with just a single TCP port exposed to the internet now

A stop gap is disabling MPTCP on your VPS now but even better is not having any public ports exposed!

quoting.text:
When I set up a new Hetzner VPS first thing I do install Tailscale and once I'm in via Tailscale lock down the firewall to only accept web traffic on HTTPS 443 for Cloudflare IPs and SSH 22 for Tailscale IP

That way nobody can get in

I know I keep repeating this but it should be basics of setting up a new VPS

So basic IMHO it should be part of any VPS service to default install Tailscale and enable it so it's the only way to get in

Why?

A VPS server is just like your laptop or destop computer but now imagine if it's connected to the entire internet with 8 billion people that can access it and try hack it

You want to only have it accessible to you

And if you want to host a website on your VPS (like I do), you should only let Cloudflare access your VPS so it can stand in front and block any hack attempts

Never expose a VPS to the world wide web which realistically is the world WILD web

text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is

Sometimes I see people calling me a grifter, saying I’m just trying to squeeze as much money as possible from my audience.

And honestly it hurts to read because it couldn’t be further from what motivates me.

We’re in the middle of an AI gold rush. Startups are raising millions, and if you have an audience in tech right now, there’s an insane amount of money to be made.

People don’t realize how many offers I turn down from companies willing to pay $5K for a single tweet promoting their product.

I could probably make a ridiculous amount of money doing this. But I’ve always refused because I don’t want my opinions to be for sale.

And I’ve seen firsthand how much brands are willing to spend on visibility with my HYROX sponsorship experiment. If money was my goal, I’d just double down on that.

The last few years have completely changed my life. I’m financially free, I have everything I need, and I genuinely don’t care about making more money just for the sake of it.

Don’t get me wrong, I LOVE making money from my apps.

Not because I need more of it, but because someone paying for something I built is the ultimate validation. It means I’ve created something valuable enough that someone is willing to pull out their credit card.

And if one person is willing to pay for it, maybe others will too. That’s what makes building businesses so exciting to me.

But what actually gets me out of bed is making weird stuff, experimenting with ideas, and seeing people use things I’ve built.

From 2015 until 2022, I was building apps alone, with barely any entrepreneur friends. I felt lonely.

Now I’ve finally found my people, made enough money to live comfortably, and get to do what I love every day.

I don’t need more. I just want to have fun building stuff with people who love it as much as I do. ❤️

text:
I made a mistake.

When Jack and I decided to organize this $100K Hackathon, my biggest concern was cheating.

Unlike a regular hackathon, everyone participates from home. And because the winner is whoever makes the most PROFIT (not revenue), there are so many ways to manipulate the numbers.

So I added a $99 entry fee.

One thing I’ve learned from building businesses is that people tend to be more committed when they pay for something.

I thought it would filter out spam, attract serious builders, and make the competition fairer for everyone.

But I completely missed the other side.

3 years ago, I was a living with my apps. Today, I’m financially free. My life changed so much that somewhere along the way, I lost perspective on what $99 means to someone else.

For someone in India, someone struggling to pay their bills, or someone trying to make their first dollar online, $99 can be a lot of money.

And those are exactly the people I want to help!

I’ve spent years sharing what I’ve learned, reviewing random people’s landing pages, and organizing free meetups around the world. Not because there’s money to make, but because I genuinely love seeing people build things and succeed.

And somehow, I was so focused on keeping cheaters out that I didn’t realize I was also keeping genuine builders out.

That’s my mistake.

So I’ve decided to make the $100K Hackathon completely FREE :)

Everyone who already paid got a full refund.

I’m still worried about cheating. That problem hasn’t disappeared, and Jack and I will have to figure out better ways to verify profits and keep the leaderboard fair.

But that’s our problem to solve.

Thank you to everyone who shared their thoughts. Sometimes you need people to remind you of things you’ve forgotten.

I genuinely hope this hackathon changes someone’s life.

❤️

I bought a pair of VIVO Barefoot shoes in Abu Dhabi 2 weeks ago for 850 AED (~$230).

I absolutely loved wearing them (you should try them!). But 2 days later, the back of one shoe broke.

Instant love-hate relationship.

So I spun up an AI agent, gave it the receipt and photos, and asked it to get me a replacement delivered to my door. Or a refund if that wasn’t possible.

Life went on. I forgot about it.

Today, I checked my bank and noticed 850 AED had landed in my account.

I opened the agent’s chat to see what happened:

1. The agent requested a replacement delivered to my door.
2. The store had stock, but Cyprus delivery stalled.
3. The agent escalated to regional and global support.
4. The store refused international exchange. The agent pushed for a remote refund.
5. The requested reply deadline passed. No answer.
6. The agent prepared Wise dispute evidence as backup. The store eventually processed the refund.
7. The money landed.

It’s crazy that I can have an army of superintelligent agents fighting for me, 24/7, while I get on with my life.

The downside: a lot of people are going to abuse this. Filing a claim has become so easy.
